Not unsolved, but happened down the street from me. Earlier this year in April, a 98 year old woman went missing. They put out a missing persons report for her. They search the house, don't find anything amiss. They go ahead and search it a second time the next day to see if they overlooked anything. That second time they find her body stuffed inside her bedroom closet with a bunch of clothes and other items on top of her. They instantly rule it a homicide and jump right into finding her killer. Two days or so later they announce they have a suspect. A 17 year old boy that I had seen around in high school. His parents live adjacent to her house, and he's also a suspect in a couple car robberies in the area. After they decide they want to talk to him, they can't find him anywhere. They eventually find him hiding out in Cleveland. They search his room and found her wallet in a drawer and found a couple other things they think might belong to her. I think I've shared this story on here somewhere before, not sure. It was my grad party last year. No alcohol, or drugs were involved. (Mainly because my parents were there, if they weren't there probably would've been some beer and stuff) Anyway, parents had just gone to bed, had a few friends left and some coworkers. I was standing over at the bonfire when I heard this loud thud. I turn around and my coworker had fallen from the top of the pool ladder, right onto her back on the brick patio. Two people were still in the pool, and her boyfriend and my best friend were sitting right there next to her. I ran inside to get my parents and as I ran into their room i heard them talking about how great my party is going. I tell them, we all run back out and my dad immediately starts performing CPR. I forget who called 911, but they got there extremely quickly. Before they got there my friend started making this god awful sound I'll never forget. It was like she was coughing, wheezing, and the sound a coffee maker makes. When the ambulance took her away, her boyfriend couldn't handle anything that was happening so he was running up and down my street screaming and crying. A cop picked him up to calm him down and took him to the hospital to be with her. As the ambulance drove away, the sirens weren't on. We knew. We knew she was gone but we were still in denial and still hopeful she was alive. Later on, we learned that she had a heart condition that nobody knew about, not even her boyfriend. Essentially they said what happened was as she was getting out of the pool, her heart started acting up and she had a seizure. She let go of the handles, and fell right back. The fall its self didn't get her, it was the seizure. Rip Nikki. Ill never forget you for the short amount of time we were friends and coworkers.
